## Summary

### What I implemented

[`packages/cli/src/collector/diff.ts`](packages/cli/src/collector/diff.ts) — a single file with three exports:

**`DiffError`** — a plain `Error` subclass that includes the base ref in its message when git commands fail.

**`parseDiff(raw)`** — line-by-line unified diff parser:
- Detects file sections by `diff --git a/X b/Y` headers
- Derives status from `new file mode` / `deleted file mode` / `rename from|to` / binary markers
- Parses `@@ -a[,b] +c[,d] @@ header` hunk headers (missing count defaults to 1)
- Tracks old/new line counters to populate `added`/`removed` arrays
- Keeps `' '`/`'+'`/`'-'` prefixed lines in `hunk.lines`; drops `\ No newline` markers and trailing empty strings (split artefacts from a trailing `\n`)

**`extractSymbols(files)`** — symbol extraction with a two-pass design (collect raws, then merge):
- Detects `function`/`class`/`const`/`route`/`env` declarations on changed lines
- Key insight: **env vars never suppress the enclosing lookup** — only a function/class/const/route own-decl does
- Enclosing lookup walks backwards through context + same-side lines; stops at column-0 closers (`}`/`)`/`]`); falls back to the hunk `header`
- Merge rule: added+removed of same (file, kind, name) → one `modified` at the added line; enclosing `modified` never replaces an existing entry

**`getDiff(base, opts?)`** — runs `git diff --unified=5 --no-color --no-ext-diff -M <base>...HEAD` and `git rev-parse HEAD` via `execa`; wraps any git failure in `DiffError` naming the base ref.

### Test & lint results
- `pnpm test`: **22/22 passed** ✅
- `pnpm lint` (tsc + prettier): **clean** ✅ (ran `pnpm format` to fix Prettier style issues)

### Uncertainties resolved during implementation
- **Enclosing + own-decl interaction**: the spec says "no function/class/const/route declaration of its own" — env vars are explicitly excluded from that gate, so a line like `dbUrl: process.env.DB_URL` still triggers enclosing lookup even though it produces an `env` symbol directly.
- **Empty trailing lines**: unified diffs end with `\n`, so `split('\n')` produces a trailing `''` that must be silently ignored (not treated as a context line that inflates hunk line counts).
